notes: The proposition asserts that the type (g,nu) of an MD-graph is anabelian, written as 2g+nu>=3. The argument on this sheet considers g=1 and nu=0, separates two possibilities using the genus sum, compares vertex and edge counts, and invokes endpoints and a circle realization. This is a description of the transcription, not an independent proof check.

The tree replacement literally says n’est réduit, with no pas. The later phrase is literally de genre nuls. Neither has been repaired for grammar or mathematical expectation. The final clause says d’ordre trois, whereas the earlier stability condition is written >=3; both forms are retained.
The compact h-index in the initial sum and the overworked value after the later h_1= remain doubtful after inspection of their whole formulas. No expected Betti-number value has been imposed.

The raised arbre parenthesis belongs after h_1=0, while Dans le premier cas has its own leader to La relation. The stability note attaches before live Mais un. The complete arbre qui…sommet phrase replaces the canceled graph description. The long leader under the no-endpoint parenthesis enters between nuls and et, and pt. attaches before bord.

The terminal point of the stability note cannot be separated securely from its leader, so the doubt is confined to that point. The bottom 15 is transcribed as pagination in light ink with unidentified authorship.

Independent audit: anabélien has the tall b/l and dotted i sequence, and the genus symbol has a separate underline. The map shaft is clear but its very small right endpoint remains arrow/minus uncertain. The canceled group following the first live h_1=1 remains +1/et uncertain. The stability insertion reads de type (1,0): the tall t and descending y/p are distinct, and the lower pair has two figures separated by a comma. It is not a reference to a numbered condition. Live Mais un is below the leader, and nuls retains its terminal s. The h-index, later h_1 value, canceled ou/comme and insertion punctuation remain doubtful. No independent proof of the proposition was performed.
